messages.subject: auto-callibration
parts:
Dear,

My cal.error.start is for some of my participants rather high (0.03) and my cal.error.end is for all participants below 0.01 (which is good?). However, I got weird results so I am exploring the auto-callibration a bit more in detail.

I tried to run my script with do.cal=TRUE (default) + ENMO=TRUE and applying the cut-points of Hildebrand. --> preferred option but weird results
I tried to run my script with do.cal=FALSE + ENMO=TRUE and applying the cut-points of Hildebrand.

However, I got exact same results where I would expect when specifying do.cal=FALSE, GGIR would not check and correct for callibration error which would produce other results? 

If 'do.cal=TRUE' and 'do.cal=FALSE' give exact the same results, it means that GGIR does not correct for the callibration error in my data which can possibly explain the weird results? (knowing that enmo is sensitive for calibration errors)

Kind regards,
Iris

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] auto-callibration
parts:
Please remove the file "results/QC/data_quality_report.csv"
and try again. GGIR automatically retrieves the calibration information from this file if present when it is told not to run the auto-calibration or when it sees that this file already holds the results from a previous attempt.

Vincent
